author: Mark Atwood
text:
Not fixable here; documented instead. Leaving this open, because the limitation is real and still present -- it is now legible rather than resolved.

Checked for an upstream fix: der 0.8.3 is the latest published version, and the restriction is deliberate, not a bug. der/src/asn1/utc_time.rs states it: 'Due to common operations working on UNIX_EPOCH, UtcTimes are only supported for the years 1970-2049', with MIN_YEAR = 1970 hardcoded in the decoder. RFC 5280 4.1.2.5.1 gives UTCTime 1950-2049, so der is narrower than the spec by design.

It cannot be worked around in this workspace. The restriction lives in the type x509-cert parses into, so the certificate fails before pkix-path sees it -- which is also why the error reads 'malformed ASN.1 DER value for UTCTime' rather than anything about validity. Fixing it means forking der or x509-cert.

What was missing was that none of this was written down anywhere a user would look. Someone handed a certificate OpenSSL reads fine, and told it is malformed DER, had nothing to go on. pkix-path's Limitations section now carries it, including that it is fail-closed, that OpenSSL disagrees so the difference is real rather than strictness, and that PKITS 4.2.3 is the one vector this crate cannot evaluate.

Deliberately did not add detection to turn the DER error into a specific one: that would be a special-case heuristic on a parse failure for a condition no conforming CA produces.
